# A loop defer f()? with a nil result leaves the error result nil and
# allocates nothing: the error result stays on the stack and the wrapper
# closure is not allocated per iteration [T-104.2]. The hand-written form
# in ./hand is the control that the -m patterns below can match.
env GOPROXY=off
env GOTOOLCHAIN=local

logos build -o $WORK/esc$GOEXE .
exec $WORK/esc$GOEXE
stdout '^ok err-nil$'
stdout '^ok loop-noalloc$'
stdout '^ok single-noalloc$'

logos build -gcflags=-m ./hand
stderr 'moved to heap: err'
stderr 'func literal escapes to heap'

logos build -gcflags=-m ./pooled
! stderr 'moved to heap: err'
! stderr 'func literal escapes to heap'

-- go.mod --
module example.com/deferesc

go 1.27

-- hand/hand.lgo --
package hand

import "errors"

//go:noinline
func closeNil() error { return nil }

func Loop(n int) (err error) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		defer func() {
			if e := closeNil(); e != nil {
				if err == nil {
					err = e
				} else {
					err = errors.Join(err, e)
				}
			}
		}()
	}
	return nil
}

-- pooled/pooled.lgo --
package pooled

//go:noinline
func closeNil() error { return nil }

func Loop(n int) (err error) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		defer closeNil()?
	}
	return nil
}

-- main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"testing"
)

var sinkErr error

//go:noinline
func closeNil() error { return nil }

func Loop(n int) (err error) {
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		defer closeNil()?
	}
	return nil
}

//go:noinline
func Single() (err error) {
	defer closeNil()?
	return nil
}

func main() {
	if err := Loop(3); err != nil {
		fmt.Println("FAIL err", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println("ok err-nil")
	if got := testing.AllocsPerRun(200, func() { sinkErr = Loop(5) }); got != 0 {
		fmt.Println("FAIL loop-noalloc", got)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println("ok loop-noalloc")
	if s := testing.AllocsPerRun(200, func() { sinkErr = Single() }); s != 0 {
		fmt.Println("FAIL single-noalloc", s)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println("ok single-noalloc")
}
